Blood. It painted the walls of the bedroom. I looked around at the aftermath. The scene of the event that would destroy everything I had ever known.

We had all grown up in a world reading books and watching movies about monsters. We dreamed about how glorious it would be to slay vampires, or decapitate zombies. Killing monsters was nothing like they made it out to be.

My eyes shot open at seven thirty in the morning. A blood curdling scream echoed through the house.

What’s happening?

I reached into the night stand and pulled out a 9mm. Was there an intruder? The screams started again. They came from my daughters room at the end of the hall. My heart leapt into my throat, my arms and legs felt like they were made of lead. I pushed the fear aside, and dove for the door. The rhythmic beating of my heart matched my pace as I tore down the hallway.

As I neared her room everything fell suddenly silent. I burst into her bedroom door, shoulder first, ripping it from the hinges. My eyes caught sight of something. The adrenaline abandoned me and I was made of lead once more.

On the floor was my wife’s body, or what was left of it at least. Her face looked as though it had been eaten off by a pack of rabid dogs. Her blood was smeared across the walls like someone had been finger painting with it, her intestines sprinkled the floor like confetti.

My mouth tasted metallic as I fought back the urge to vomit. Tears blurred my vision. What kind of sick monster could do this? I had to look the bastard in the eyes before I slowly, painfully ended his life.

I raised my gaze. There it was tearing away chunks of flesh with its hands and mouth. It wasn’t a man, or a pack of rabid dogs. No. I couldn’t get that lucky. My three year old daughter crouched over her mother’s remains, blood up to her elbows, and smeared across her mouth like barbecue sauce.

She stopped mid meal and glared at me with cold, dead eyes. Her head gave a sort of twitching jerk as she began gnashing her teeth. Bits of my wife falling out of her mouth.

She lunged at me. I raised my pistol. As tears clouded my vision once more I whispered, “Daddy loves you…” and squeezed the trigger. Her tiny body crumpled to the floor as the bullet pierced her skull. I fell with her, convulsing and sobbing.

I didn’t do it because I knew what she was. I did it, because the moment I saw her eyes I knew my sweet, little Tabby was dead. I knew it wasn’t her. The movies never told us about this. They never showed the hero sobbing and vomiting after shooting his own child. The movies lied.
